A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WIMHF study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of seven preference datasets, feature validation, reward-model data-curation experiments, and personalized preference prediction.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds decomposition ablations, feature-count sensitivity, embedding and seed robustness, and prompt-conditioning results.

M1.justification: The embedding-difference inputs, signed Matryoshka BatchTopK SAE, feature interpretation and filtering, preference regressions, and personalization procedure remain unchanged. Alternative decompositions and embeddings are evaluated as diagnostic variants; they do not replace the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven preference datasets, RewardBench2 evaluation, and Community Alignment personalization task. The additions vary representations and model configurations within existing coverage; no new language, population, dataset, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 adds Embed-TopDims and Embed-PCA as evaluated alternatives to the SAE across all seven datasets. This introduces a substantive comparison against simpler feature decompositions, beyond the retained ICAI and black-box prediction comparisons.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols include an M = 16, 32, 64, 128 sweep, decomposition comparisons with 32 features and shared interpretation procedures, cosine-based feature matching, and prompt-interaction evaluation. Existing preprocessing, reward-model training settings, and application-evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands checks of the method's design choices: Appendix A tests feature-count sensitivity, replaces the SAE with simpler decompositions, and examines embedding-model and seed robustness. Appendix E adds prompt-interaction analysis. These supplement the existing human validation and subjectivity-estimator checks.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 newly reports two independently seeded SAE training runs on HH-RLHF and compares their features qualitatively. Existing bootstrap confidence intervals, significance tests, and multiple-testing corrections are retained; the PDFs do not establish increased repetitions for the original headline experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial validation outcomes: Table 2 reports mean fidelity of 0.33 for SAE, 0.20 for Embed-TopDims, and 0.13 for Embed-PCA; further additions report width sensitivity, matched features, and prompt-interaction results, including HH-RLHF AUC of 0.647 versus 0.674 under different inputs. Original benchmark and application results remain unchanged. Figure 5's caption changes from 59.9%/33.7% to 60.4%/33.3%, matching the already-existing plot and main text.

T1.justification: The dataset factorization, SAE loss, fidelity and marginal-effect definitions, and mixed-effects and personalization equations remain equivalent. The added material provides empirical analyses and discussion, without new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, principal contributions, and application claims remain stable. The conclusion removes the broad 'Unlike prior methods' novelty contrast and instead states superiority over a prior prompting-based method, modestly narrowing the contribution framing.

C2.justification: New Appendix E specifies limitations concerning prompt-dependent correctness, English-only validation, and personalization restricted to one dataset with sparse per-user observations. v2 also discusses the coverage-versus-redundancy tradeoff when increasing feature count and qualifies significant-feature counts as an incomplete measure of practical usefulness in the ICAI comparison.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository pointer beneath the abstract and documents the ModernBERT model identifier and feature-matching procedure for the new robustness tests. Existing training, hardware, preprocessing, and prompt disclosures are retained. The repository's contents or accessibility cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Christian et al. on reward-model token interpretability and Jiang et al. on interpretable embeddings, while removing Ge et al. on alignment axioms. Section 6 explicitly distinguishes analysis of underlying feedback data from reward-model token probing; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized wording corrections, more cautious 'predict' terminology, conference header and author formatting, and new appendix subsections; the former supplementary Appendix E becomes Appendix F.

P2.justification: The document adopts conference typography, running headers, and substantially different text and float placement throughout. Three new tables display the ablation and robustness results. Existing figures and tables are retained but resized or regrouped, including Figures 4 and 5 sharing a page and Figure 8 appearing alongside the sustainability examples.

improvement.justification: The new decomposition comparisons and sensitivity checks strengthen support for design choices that v1 justified largely qualitatively. Explicit applicability limits, the code pointer, and the corrected Figure 5 caption improve transparency and consistency. The gains are bounded: central findings remain unchanged, and embedding/seed robustness evidence consists of qualitative examples from HH-RLHF rather than broad quantitative validation.
